sources.title: David Kirsh : My Lab
sources.text: Home Research Publications Classes Consulting My Lab Interactive Cognition Lab We do basic research on the topics needed for designing interactive environments. These include studying the nature of Distributed Collaboration, Interactivity, Coordination, Human Computer Interaction, Representation, E-Learning, Attention Management and how to increase the Context Awareness of our environments. Projects include: Augmented Video - how to add sound and annotation to share knowledge better Design of collaborative environments Context Aware Offices Elearning Information Architecture [ Visit lab website ]

sources.text: Home Research Publications Classes Consulting My Lab Files David Kirsh Phone (858) 822-2475 Lab CSB 205-206 Office CSB 172 kirsh at ucsd.edu D r. David Kirsh, Professor/past chair of the Dept. of Cognitive Science/UCSD, received a D. Phil.(Oxford), did post-doctoral work at MIT (AI Lab), held research or Visiting Professor positions at MIT and Stanford, and the Bartlett School of Architecture UCL. He has written on situated and embodied cognition, how environments can be shaped to simplify/extend cognition, and how space, external representations, our bodies and even manipulable objects become interactive tools for thought. He is co-Director of the Arthur C. Clarke Center for Human Imagination and on the Board of Directors for the Academy of Neuroscience for Architecture. He is Adjunct Professor at Trinity Laban Conservatoire of Music and Dance.
